Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 68
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: European
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Politician
  trauma_type: Life-threatening accident
  pcl5: 73

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Discomfort: Feeling uncomfortable, Olfactory (Alcohol): Alcohol smell, Crash Imagery: Cars hit by accident
  Maladaptive Strategies: Self-Blame Rumination: I dwell on what I have done wrong, Rumination: Self-Blame: repeatedly blame myself for what happened, Avoid Driving: Driving or being a passenger in a vehicle
  Threat: Waking Alert: I wake during the night to check whether I am safe, Threat in Silence: Unusual silence makes me feel something dangerous is about to happen, Concentration: Having difficulty concentrating
  Memory: Snapshot Memory: I remember the frightening event as a few moments, and each moment is a picture in my mind., Cannot Explain Clearly: When I try to explain what happened I lose the thread and cannot finish, Pain Recall: When the memory returns I feel physical pain in the same parts of my body as during the event
  Negative Appraisals: Character Blame: The event happened to me because of the sort of person I am, Hypervigilance: I have to be on guard all the time, Exposed to Others: I feel that others can see what happened to me just by looking at me

Vignette:
Giorgio's life took a dramatic turn two years ago when his car skidded off the road on a rainy evening. The accident left him with severe injuries and an indelible memory of the moment his vehicle crashed into a tree. He recalls it as a series of snapshots, each one frozen in time - the screeching tires, the shattered windshield, and the feeling of weightlessness before impact. When memories resurface, Giorgio's body responds with physical pain in the same areas where he was injured. As a seasoned politician, Giorgio had always been comfortable in the public eye. However, since the accident, he has become increasingly self-conscious about being seen in public. He feels exposed, as if others can see the traumatic event etched on his face, and this fear drives him to avoid crowded areas and public appearances whenever possible. Giorgio's self-blame rumination began soon after the accident, with thoughts of "What was I thinking, driving so fast?" or "If only I had taken that turn slower." These ruminations have become a constant companion, often waking him up during the night to replay the events leading up to the crash. His mind is consumed by self-doubt and criticism, making it challenging for him to concentrate on his work as a politician. The smell of alcohol has also become a potent trigger, instantly transporting Giorgio back to that fateful evening when he had been driving after attending a dinner party where wine was served. The pungent aroma now fills him with anxiety, and he finds himself avoiding social gatherings or events where drinks are served. Driving has become another source of distress for Giorgio. He avoids getting behind the wheel whenever possible and feels uneasy as a passenger in someone else's car. Seeing cars damaged in accidents or hearing about similar incidents on the news triggers vivid imagery of his own crash, leaving him shaken. Giorgio has always been a man who thrives on being in control, but since the accident, he has become hypervigilant, constantly scanning his surroundings for potential dangers. He wakes up multiple times during the night to check whether everything is safe and secure, often getting out of bed to ensure all doors and windows are locked. Despite his efforts to maintain a sense of normalcy, Giorgio's life has undergone significant changes since the accident. His marriage has become strained as he struggles to connect with his wife on an intimate level, feeling like he is living in a constant state of vulnerability. He has also had to scale back his public appearances and delegate more tasks to his colleagues due to his difficulty concentrating. One evening, after attending a meeting at city hall, Giorgio was overcome by the familiar sensation of discomfort that usually precedes an anxiety attack. As he walked out into the silence of the night, he felt an eerie sense of foreboding wash over him, as if something terrible was about to happen. It was then that he realized he could no longer keep living in this state of heightened alertness and decided to seek help. Giorgio's main hope is to learn how to break free from the grip of his traumatic memories and regain a sense of control over his life. He fears that if he doesn't address these issues, they will continue to erode his relationships and undermine his ability to function as a politician. As he sits in his therapist's office, he knows it won't be easy, but he is willing to confront the darkness head-on to find some measure of peace and reclaim his life.
